Article Title: When Sonia met Rajiv: Congress leader narrates her 1st meeting with husband in X debut
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi makes X debut, recalls first meeting with Rajiv Gandhi ahead of book launch

Sonia Gandhi recalls meeting Rajiv Gandhi in Cambridge

Upcoming memoir traces her personal journey

NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi made her debut on social media platform X on Saturday, sharing a video in which she recalled her first meeting with former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and offered a glimpse of her upcoming book, Belonging: A Journey of Love.The book, Sonia Gandhi's first, is scheduled to be launched on November 10. It recounts her personal journey, including her memories with Rajiv Gandhi and experiences from her younger days to the present.In the nearly two-minute video accompanying her first post on X, Sonia Gandhi recalled meeting Rajiv Gandhi at the Varsity Restaurant, a Greek eatery in Cambridge, England, where they were students.The video featured photographs of the couple and the restaurant where they first met."In a small Greek restaurant in Cambridge, my journey of love began. Rajiv and I created a world filled with love, laughter and memories. On 10th November, I share that world with you," she wrote in her post.Speaking in the video, the Congress MP recalled looking for Italian food while living in England, where she said the food available at the time did not suit her preferences."Food in England in those days was awful. In those days, you didn't have so many restaurants, you know, like you have today," she said.She explained that she was looking for a place serving food closer to what she was accustomed to, particularly Italian cuisine, when she discovered the Greek restaurant."And then, we discovered this place (Varsity Restaurant). It was a Greek restaurant where many European students, but also Indian students, used to go for their meals. And that is then where I met Rajiv in that very restaurant," she said.Recalling her first impression of Rajiv Gandhi, she said she felt almost immediately that he was someone she would want to spend her life with."When I first met him, I felt almost immediately that you know he was someone I would really love to be with. And, of course, I learned that it was the same for him," she said.Sonia Gandhi also recalled that a common friend introduced them. The two subsequently became friends and began attending parties with other students and visiting places together."I remember when I first met him, a friend, a common friend, introduced us. Then, you know, we became friends. Then going to parties with friends, or going to see sights, or… We went to a Valentine party where there were lots of students," she said.Describing what stood out to her about Rajiv Gandhi, she said his gentle nature had left a lasting impression."He was a very gentle-looking person. Of course, he was very good-looking. But that gentleness came through. So that was something which really touched me and struck me. So that, of course, I'll never forget when I first met him," she said.Sonia married Rajiv Gandhi on February 25, 1968.The upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, explores Sonia Gandhi's life, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance with Rajiv Gandhi to her move to India and the personal losses that shaped her life and relationship with her adopted country.Her debut on X comes two days after she joined Instagram on Thursday and shared a video offering a first look at the book.In her first Instagram post, she expressed gratitude at being able to share the preview with readers and described the memoir as a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong."I look forward to sharing it with you," she wrote in the post.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi makes her debut on social media platform X on Saturday. She shared a video in which she recalled her first meeting with Rajiv Gandhi. She also offered a glimpse of her upcoming book, Belonging: A Journey of Love. The book, Sonia Gandhi's first, is scheduled to be launched on November 10.

Article Title: 'Will not sign': AISA chief Neha Bora defies Delhi police peace bond notice after HC setback
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association president Neha Bora on Saturday said she would not sign a bond to "keep peace" before a special executive magistrate, a day after the Delhi high court dismissed her plea challenging the police notice directing her to furnish a Rs 10,000 bond with a surety."We don't have any conditions. We are not going to sign the bond," Bora said.Bora had moved the high court, arguing that the notice was vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by material establishing the likelihood of a breach of peace.She alleged that the proceedings were a "colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of Constitution".During Thursday's hearing, Bora's counsel argued that citizens did not need permission to hoist the national flag, referring to the police notice alleging that she had hoisted it without valid permission.The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directed Bora to appear before the magistrate on October 19 and explain why she should not execute a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with one surety "for keeping peace for a period of enquiry".Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Central Park in Connaught Place. She was released the following day.According to her petition, the police initiated proceedings over alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and allegations that she had instigated people to join a demonstration at Connaught Place that day."The impugned notice rests on a prima facie incorrect fact, namely that the petitioner instigated people to participate in the demonstration at Central Park, CP on Oct 16. The petitioner's call and the incident alleged were different. The petitioner called for a peaceful gathering at Mandi House at 5.00 pm on Oct 16, and it is a matter of record that she was detained from Mandi House," Bora's petition stated.
Article Summary: All India Students' Association president Neha Bora says she will not sign a bond to "keep peace" before a special executive magistrate. Delhi high court dismissed her plea challenging the police notice directing her to furnish a Rs 10,000 bond with a surety. Bora had moved the high court, arguing that the notice was vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by material establishing the likelihood of a breach of peace.

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday said the expansion and reshuffle of his cabinet would take place in the first two to three days of next week.Talking to reporters, the J&K chief minister said he had met lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha and sought time for the exercise."Yes, it (reshuffle) certainly was (discussed). Article Title: Arms training case: US mercenary VanDyke, 6 Ukrainians to remain abroad till Feb 24
Article Text:
VanDyke, 6 Ukrainians to remain abroad till Feb 24

NEW DELHI: An NIA court Friday allowed US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals accused in the Myanmar arms training case to remain in their home countries till Feb 24. The permission came after NIA told special judge Prashant Sharma of Rouse Avenue court that it needed more time to probe the UA(P)A offences against them.“Further probe is ongoing and more time is required in order to ascertain and verify the facts about the commission of offences under UA(P)A in view of import and recovery of huge quantities of drones and accessories through India,” it said.VanDyke attended the court hearing Friday and sought the release of his seized personal articles. The seven accused had earlier sought six weeks to meet their families and were allowed to stay abroad till Oct 23. They were arrested on March 13 for allegedly training insurgent-linked groups in Myanmar.
Article Summary: US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke and 6 Ukrainians to remain abroad till Feb 24. They were arrested on March 13 for allegedly training insurgent-linked groups in Myanmar. The seven accused had earlier sought six weeks to meet their families and were allowed to stay abroad till Oct 23.

Article Title: UP polls: Congress shares initial list with SP, seeks 175-200 seats
Article Text:
Scepticism within SP over Congress’ seat demands

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

How the change in UP Congress leadership could influence seat-sharing talks

NEW DELHI: The Congress has formally begun seat-sharing negotiations with the Samajwadi Party (SP) in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, submitting an initial list of more than 175 assembly constituencies to the Akhilesh Yadav-led party.Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congress’ in-charge for Uttar Pradesh, told PTI that the list was shared with SP leaders around two days ago. He added that leaders from both parties would soon hold detailed discussions on the nature of a seat-sharing arrangement.“I can't give you the exact numbers, but we have submitted a list for 175 to 200 seats. The leadership of both parties will sit together to thrash out the nitty-gritties of the seat-sharing arrangement," Gautam said.The Congress has reportedly classified constituencies based on an assessment of its electoral prospects, and seat-sharing negotiations are expected to centre on this assessment.However, several SP leaders remain unconvinced that the Congress has enough political clout to demand 175-200 seats, despite their successful alliance in Uttar Pradesh during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.The scepticism stems from the Congress’ declining electoral fortunes in Uttar Pradesh since 1989, when it last held power in the country’s most populous state.“I think our party leader Akhilesh Yadav has made it clear that winnability is the sole criterion (for contesting the polls). Anyone can demand anything, but in politics, to reach an acceptable and meaningful solution, you have to move beyond posturing,” a senior SP leader told PTI.The Congress contested the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections independently but managed to win just two constituencies, down from seven in 2017, when it fought in alliance with the SP. That year, the SP lost power after a single term, securing only 47 seats, while the BJP won a landslide 312 seats in the 403-member ssembly.In 2022, the BJP retained power with 255 seats, while the SP won 111 constituencies.However, the 2024 Lok Sabha elections offered the Congress renewed hope. The grand old party won six seats in Uttar Pradesh, while the SP secured 37 of the state’s 80 seats, limiting the BJP to 33, down from 62 in 2019 and 71 in 2014. The results have strengthened the Congress’ expectations of securing a “respectable share” of seats in the 2027 assembly elections, party leaders acknowledged.“It’s obvious… The 2024 Lok Sabha results were proof that together the two parties can make an impact. In politics, there has to be room for meaningful give and take,” a senior Congress leader said.The recent leadership change in the Uttar Pradesh Congress, with Aradhana Misra “Mona” succeeding Ajay Rai as state unit chief, is also believed to have been factored into the party’s efforts to reach an amicable seat-sharing arrangement with the SP.Some believe Rai was not in favour of a pre-poll alliance, viewing a post-poll arrangement as a more suitable option for the Congress.However, some party leaders feel that Misra’s “excellent relations” with the SP leadership may have influenced the party’s decision to appoint her months ahead of the assembly elections, potentially facilitating negotiations between themThe Uttar Pradesh assembly elections are scheduled to be held in February-March next year.
Article Summary: The Congress has submitted an initial list of more than 175 assembly constituencies to the Akhilesh Yadav-led party. Several SP leaders remain unconvinced that the Congress has enough political clout to demand 175-200 seats. The Congress contested the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections independently but managed to win just two constituencies, down from seven in 2017.

Article Title: Fodder scam accused nabbed after 25 years, had fled to Nepal
Article Text:
Ending a quarter-century-long game of hide-and-seek, CBI has arrested Satyendra Kumar

NEW DELHI: Ending a quarter-century-long game of hide-and-seek, CBI has arrested Satyendra Kumar , a key fugitive wanted in connection with Bihar’s infamous Fodder scam . The suspect had fled to Nepal and was tracked down during a train journey he took upon returning to India, the agency said.Acting on court orders, CBI had undertaken the probe into the multi-crore corruption scam involving the systematic embezzlement of funds from the Animal Husbandry Department in Bihar during the 1990s. High-profile political figures, including former Bihar chief minister Lalu Prasad Yadav, along with several senior bureaucrats and suppliers, have since been convicted in multiple cases related to illegal treasury withdrawals. The agency had filed dozens of FIRs to untangle a nexus of politicians, bureaucrats, suppliers and middlemen who siphoned off public funds through fake invoices for cattle feed, medicines and equipment.Kumar, alleged to be a supplier, had been on the run since 2001, vanishing into the shadows immediately after the agency filed its charge sheet in the case. His persistent failure to face trial prompted the court to issue an arrest warrant and declare him an absconder, cementing his status as one of the scam’s most elusive figures.It was a to a manhunt that spanned more than two decades across international borders. For over 25 years, Kumar managed to evade the law by taking refuge across the border in Nepal living under an assumed identity. However, the net slowly began to tighten as CBI officials mounted human and technical surveillance to pinpoint his exact movements.The breakthrough came when intelligence revealed that Kumar had re-entered India and was travelling by train from Guna, Madhya Pradesh, to Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Acting swiftly on the input, a team was tasked with intercepting the fugitive mid-transit. Units were deployed across Lucknow Railway Station well before the train arrived. Around midnight on Oct 22, the CBI managed to take the accused into custody and placed him under arrest. He was taken to Ranchi on transit remand, where he will finally be produced before the court to face trial.
Article Summary: CBI has arrested Satyendra Kumar, a key fugitive wanted in connection with Bihar’s infamous Fodder scam. The suspect had fled to Nepal and was tracked down during a train journey he took upon returning to India. Kumar, alleged to be a supplier, had been on the run since 2001.

NEW DELHI: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday spoke with singer Daler Mehndi over the phone, days after a controversy erupted over a cabinet minister reprimanding the singer on stage during an event.According to the CMO, Dhami inquired about Mehndi's well-being and told the artiste that Uttarakhand upholds the rich tradition of 'Atithi Devo Bhava'."Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami spoke with singer Daler Mehndi over the phone to inquire about his well-being. Article Title: 'Lot of pressure on him, happened in just 2 hrs': Robert Vadra on son Raihan’s Bikaner exhibition row
Article Text:
Artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, the son of Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Robert Vadra, during his solo exhibition at Bikaner House, in New Delhi.

‘All 75 had to be taken down’

NEW DELHI: Businessman Robert Vadra has alleged that pressure was exerted on his son, artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, to remove photographs documenting recent protests in Delhi from his solo exhibition at Bikaner House, with the intervention coming just hours before the scheduled opening.Calling the episode shocking, Robert said the authorities had received the exhibition’s PDF a week in advance and had raised no objections until the final hours. He also praised Raihan for proceeding with the exhibition despite the removal of several photographs.“There was a lot of pressure on him to remove everything, and this happened just two hours before the opening of his exhibition. It was shocking because the authorities had received the PDF file a week in advance and had been informed about the exhibition,” Robert said.He said setting up an exhibition required considerable effort and that officials had visited the venue, seen the displays and raised no objections initially. However, the situation changed shortly before the opening, he alleged, without any explanation.“Despite this, I think he was brave enough to go ahead with the exhibition using whatever remained. As I said, I am proud of him. Everyone who had been invited attended the exhibition because this is also his profession,” he said.In a separate statement, Robert said Raihan had worked hard on the exhibition, which drew on photographs he took while documenting protests in the national capital.“I am very proud of my son, Raihan, for the hard work he puts in every time he takes up a subject that is relevant to what is happening around him,” he said.Robert said Raihan had attended the protests, keeping his friends in mind and considering the support students needed. He carried his camera to the demonstrations, captured photographs and expressions, and later decided to organise an exhibition on the subject.According to Robert, Raihan submitted a PDF of the proposed exhibition to Bikaner House officials about a week before the event. He alleged that the authorities did not raise concerns about the material at the time.However, in the final 24 hours, after Raihan and his team had spent considerable time setting up the exhibition, officials arrived to review the displays, Robert said. The commissioner of Bikaner House subsequently told them that certain displays would have to be removed.“When Raihan asked how many displays were an issue and offered to remove any that were considered controversial, he was told that all 75 had to be taken down,” Robert alleged.Robert also questioned the decision to remove the photographs, saying artistic expression should be allowed in a democracy. He pointed out that Bikaner House comes under the Rajasthan government.“If we believe in democracy, there is no point in mixing politics with the creative world. Everyone should be allowed to express themselves,” he said.The controversy centres on Raihan’s solo exhibition,, after he alleged that more than 70 photographs documenting recent youth-led protests in Delhi were removed shortly before the exhibition opened. Bikaner House has said certain photographs were inconsistent with its policy, which it said focuses on culture and wildlife, and that the removed images carried political messaging.
Article Summary: Businessman Robert Vadra has alleged that pressure was exerted on his son, artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, to remove photographs. The intervention came just hours before the scheduled opening of his solo exhibition at Bikaner House. Robert said the authorities had received the exhibition’s PDF a week in advance and had raised no objections until the final hours.

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi launched a fresh attack on Rahul Gandhi and Congress, saying the opposition party is endangering India’s achievements, strengths and progress to shield the Nehru-Gandhi family from its repeated electoral “failures” and is trying to defame the country by seeking help from foreign forces.“Dimagi naxals have captured Congress so much that it has lost its ability to think. Those who used to cause destruction in forests are now determined to wreak havoc on the country through Congress,” he said, while addressing the NDTV World Summit, referring to hardcore Left elements accused of being sympathetic to Maoists and now vocal in protests against EC and govt.“Congress makes more failed attempts to launch its neta (Rahul) than the launches from Sriharikota (Isro satellite launch site) in a year,” he said.“No one knows how long Congress will stake the country’s future to launch its failed product,” he added. “Grapes have become so sour for Congress that it is cutting off the grapevine. This family of Congress has become a burden for its own party.” The PM added that many seasoned functionaries of the party realise this but prefer to keep quiet while feeling insulted.At a time of so much disorder in the world, a message of a strong India should go out.But some people are dreaming of stoking disorder in the country. “These people go abroad to seek foreign intervention to defame India,” he said, bringing up a charge BJP repeatedly levels against Rahul.Also Read: In call with Bibi, PM Modi says urgent need to restore West Asia peace Congress’s single-minded determination to buttress the Gandhi family, he said, is not only a threat to democracy but also comes at the cost of his govt’s hon­est critics whose voice is suppressed by the main opposition party and is drowned out in its noise.Many opposition MPs, he said, want to be heard in Parliament but Congress in its zeal to keep the family in the limelight, does not allow it to function by resorting to disruptions. He said agitations highlighting govt’s shortcomings and wanting to reform the system are necessary in a democracy but Congress wants to destroy them.Turning to his call for Viksit Bharat by 2047, Modi said the spirit of “we will do it” is echoing in the country and highlighted his govt’s efforts to turn India into the “brain office” of the world from its earlier image of merely a global back office.He said India stands for a world order rooted in humanity and not promoting big powers at the cost of small powers.The country followed this during the Covid-19 pandemic when global powers prioritised their selfish interests, he said.“India’s role and identity are changing. The world that used to depend on its manpower is now also trusting its brainpower,” the PM said, citing the strides the country is making in the AI and semiconductor industry.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi says Congress is endangering India's achievements, strengths and progress to shield the Nehru-Gandhi family from its repeated electoral “failures” “Dimagi naxals have captured Congress so much that it has lost its ability to think,” he said, referring to hardcore Left elements.

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: How Tom Brady stepped up to provide 750,000 meals to children, families and senior citizens in need across Tampa Bay
Article Text:
Tom Brady (Getty Images)

Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen donated 750,000 meals in Tampa Bay

Tom Brady's Tampa Bay move came during a difficult period

In 2020, as the COVID-19 pandemic brought daily life to a standstill, Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen used their resources to help families facing food shortages in Florida. The NFL legend had just begun a new chapter with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after spending two decades with the New England Patriots. Yet, amid the excitement surrounding his move, Brady and his wife turned their attention to a more urgent issue. Their contribution helped fund 750,000 meals for people in need, offering support to children, families and senior citizens during one of the most difficult periods in recent history.The donation came shortly after Brady and Bündchen relocated to the Tampa area in 2020. Their support went to Feeding Tampa Bay, an organisation that provides food assistance across a 10-county region in Florida.The organisation announced the contribution on social media, welcoming the couple and thanking them for supporting local residents."We welcome @TomBrady, @giseleofficial and their family to our community and thank them as they #StandwithFTB by providing 750,000 meals to support our children, families and seniors throughout the 10-county region that we serve," the organisation wrote.The timing made the contribution particularly significant.Schools across the United States had closed or changed their operations to limit the spread of the virus. As a result, many children who relied on school breakfasts and lunches faced uncertainty over their next meals.Feeding Tampa Bay responded by expanding its support through mobile pantries and other food assistance programmes. Its work helped reach households struggling with the sudden economic and social effects of the pandemic.For Brady and Bündchen, the donation also marked an early effort to support the community they were preparing to call home.Brady's arrival in Florida attracted considerable attention. After 20 seasons with the New England Patriots, the quarterback signed a two-year contract worth $50 million with the Buccaneers in March 2020.The move brought an end to one of the most successful partnerships between a player and an NFL franchise. Brady had won six Super Bowl titles with New England and now faced the challenge of building a new legacy in Tampa Bay.Away from football, the quarterback and Bündchen were settling into their new surroundings. The couple rented an estate owned by former New York Yankees shortstop Derek Jeter while beginning their life in Florida.However, the pandemic quickly made community support a priority. With families facing job losses, school closures and growing financial pressure, food assistance organisations had to meet rising needs.Brady and Bündchen's contribution offered practical help at a time when many households were struggling to manage basic expenses. It also showed how public figures could support local organisations already working on the front lines of a crisis.Their 2020 donation remains a notable example of the couple's charitable involvement, bringing attention to food insecurity when communities across the United States needed help the most.
Article Summary: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen donated 750,000 meals in Tampa Bay. The NFL legend had just begun a new chapter with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after spending two decades with the New England Patriots. The donation came shortly after Brady and his wife relocated to the Tampa area in 2020.

Article Title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' $325 million KC Current get a major boost with late-season surge

Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes (Instagram)

The Kansas City Current are finding their best form at a crucial point in the season, giving co-owners Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes plenty of reason to feel optimistic. With the NWSL playoffs approaching, Kansas City has climbed into fourth place after a convincing road victory over Utah. Haley Hopkins has emerged as a key attacking force, while the team's recent performances suggest that its earlier struggles may finally be behind it. The timing could hardly be better, with a top-four finish offering the Current a valuable chance to host a playoff match.The KC Current have made a strong push towards the postseason after a difficult stretch threatened to derail their campaign. Their 2-0 victory over the Utah Royals marked another important step, moving the team into fourth place with only two regular-season matches remaining.The Current have scored 11 goals and conceded just two across their last three games. Their involvement connects the club to one of the city's most prominent sporting families, while the Current continue to build their own identity through performances on the pitch.A top-four finish would allow Kansas City to host a playoff game during the November 5-7 weekend. The team also has several routes to securing a postseason place, making its upcoming home match against the Washington Spirit particularly important.Hopkins has become one of the Current's most important players at exactly the right time. The striker has scored six goals and provided an assist across the team's last three matches, taking her season tally to 11 goals and four assists.Her growing influence has helped Kansas City spread the scoring responsibility across its attack. Temwa Chawinga remains a major threat, but Hopkins' finishing, aerial ability and work rate have added another dimension to the team's forward line.Head coach Chris Armas has praised her ability to find scoring positions and lead the press.“She arrives in those areas, players put the ball in those areas, and she also leads our press from up high.”Since Ally Sentnor's departure in a trade with Angel City, Hopkins has stepped into a larger role and delivered consistently. Article Title: 'Four years, I never chased this Indian jersey': Bhuvneshwar Kumar credits IPL for India comeback
Article Text:
Bhuvneshwar Kumar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Adapting to modern T20 cricket

India pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar believes staying focused on his work without expecting too much from himself helped him deal with a four-year absence from international cricket. The experienced bowler returned to the national setup earlier this month as a replacement for injured Arshdeep Singh in the fifth T20I against the West Indies, but rain washed out the match. He eventually returned to action in the first T20I against New Zealand.Speaking in a video shared by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), Bhuvneshwar explained that focusing on the present instead of worrying about a comeback helped him grow as a player and person.“The headspace I am in is very simple. I have no expectations of myself. I think that’s how things worked out for me in the last 3-4 years. No expectations; just keep doing your work. Generally, we talk about being present; we don’t think about the future. I think that’s the headspace I am in right now. And that has happened in the last 3-4 years,” he said.Bhuvneshwar said the years away from international cricket taught him patience and maturity. Rather than constantly chasing a place in the Indian team, he concentrated on improving his game through the IPL and domestic cricket.“Four years, I never chased this Indian jersey. So honestly, I didn’t even know when those four years would come.I think it evolved big time, and I think IPL has a big role in that.”Despite having no clear expectations about his future, the 36-year-old continued working on his fitness, skills and mental preparation. He also expressed surprise at winning two IPL titles in two years.Bhuvneshwar acknowledged that T20 cricket has changed considerably, with batters attacking from the first ball and scores of 200 becoming increasingly common. However, he believes bowlers can still control the game by using smart strategies and making batters hit where they want.He also pointed out that overseas tours, particularly to SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia), present challenges because conditions often offer limited help to bowlers. According to him, success in these conditions requires maturity, careful planning and teamwork.Reflecting on India's opening win against New Zealand, Bhuvneshwar said a strong start could boost confidence across the squad and help the team perform better throughout the tour and in other formats.
Article Summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar believes staying focused on his work helped him deal with a four-year absence from international cricket. The experienced bowler returned to the national setup earlier this month as a replacement for injured Arshdeep Singh. He eventually returned to action in the first T20I against New Zealand.

Article Title: IND vs NZ 2nd T20I: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in playing XI, but there's a twist
Article Text:
Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (BCCI Photo)

Iyer explains India's decision to bowl

New Zealand make one change

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India vs New Zealand 2nd T20I : Playing XIs

India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl against New Zealand in the second T20 International on Saturday.India made two changes to their playing XI. Injured Ishan Kishan was replaced by 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, while Prince Yadav came in for Mayank Yadav.Iyer confirmed that Sooryavanshi would bat at No. 3 and not open the innings. India will continue with Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson as their opening pair.Iyer said the possibility of dew was one of the reasons behind India's decision to bowl first. He also stressed the need to maintain the aggressive approach that helped the team in the first T20I."We're going to bowl first. Yes, absolutely. That's one of the reasons (On dew being a factor). We have had a little bit of time to recover and catch up on some sleep. Everyone is in decent shape, I would say. Some of the players, including myself, do their training on match day. So, we are in a good place. It is important to maintain the aggression and repeat the things we did well in the first game," Shreyas Iyer said during the toss.The Indian captain also pointed out the need to improve the team's fielding and avoid mistakes in the final overs."In addition, we need to be proactive in the field and ensure we don't have an extra fielder inside the circle, especially in the last over. Ishan is injured, so Vaibhav comes in for him. Prince comes in for Mayank, which is just a tactical change. He is going to bat at number three (on Vaibhav's batting position)," the Indian skipper said.New Zealand also made a change to their playing XI, with Jacob Duffy replacing Adam Milne.Captain Mitchell Santner said his team had taken positives from the first T20I despite losing the match in the final over. He added that the team needed to improve its execution in key moments."(On the 1st T20I) They are a very good team, and I think we missed the mark slightly. That comes from the way they approach their game. It was a great game of cricket in the end. Losing in the last over is disappointing, but there were obviously many positives. We need to execute the small details better and see what happens," Mitchell Santner said.Santner said the players had been given time to rest after returning to their hotel late at night. With matches coming thick and fast, the team wanted to make sure everyone was ready for the second T20I."(On the preparation for this match) Training was optional. We had a morning session, and we only got back here around 2 a.m. Therefore, it was a day to refresh, especially with the games coming thick and fast. I think the guys rested well and should be ready to go today," he said.The New Zealand captain also explained that Duffy's inclusion was part of the team's rotation policy and was not linked to Milne's performance."(On the changes) Duffy comes in for Milne. With the number of games we have coming up, not just T20s but one-day internationals as well, there will be some rotation among the senior players, especially with a lot of Test cricket coming up.It is nothing to do with performance; it is just a bit of rotation, and we will see what Duffy can do tonight," Santner added.India: Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Naman Dhir, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav.New Zealand: Finn Allen, Tim Seifert (wk), Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Bevon Jacobs, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Nathan Smith, Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy, Lockie Ferguson.
Article Summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl against New Zealand. Injured Ishan Kishan was replaced by 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Prince Yadav came in for Mayank Yadav. New Zealand also made a change to their playing XI, with Jacob Duffy replacing Adam Milne.

Article Title: “So you see a lot of that inequality”: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders unionize after years of pay disputes as collective bargaining begins
Article Text:
Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders unionize after years of pay disputes as collective bargaining begins(Getty)

Dallas Cowboys recognize cheerleaders’ union after years of pay concerns

Netflix series put Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders’ pay fight in spotlight

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have taken a major step in their fight for better pay. Recently, the Cowboys agreed to recognize the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association as the squad’s collective bargaining representative. The decision gives the cheerleaders a formal voice in negotiations with the NFL franchise after years of debate over their compensation.The move comes after the Netflix series America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders brought their working lives and financial struggles to a wider audience. While the squad received a major pay increase in 2025, union recognition opens a new chapter in its push for better workplace terms.The Cowboys and the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association announced the agreement in a joint statement on Friday. The statement praised the squad’s talent and dedication and described the cheerleaders as an important part of the organization.The recognition clears the way for collective bargaining, which allows representatives to negotiate employment terms on behalf of the group. However, the announcement did not outline a new pay deal or confirm specific benefits.Those details will depend on negotiations between the two sides.The development follows years of scrutiny over cheerleader compensation. In 2018, former Cowboys cheerleader Erica Wilkins filed a lawsuit over her pay. The case ended in a 2019 settlement that doubled the squad’s per-game pay from $200 to $400.That increase marked a significant change, but it did not end questions about how much cheerleaders earned for their work. Their responsibilities extend beyond performing during NFL games, with rehearsals, appearances and other duties also demanding time and effort.Virginia Commonwealth University professor Victor Chen, who studies labor issues as a sociologist said that Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders were likely helped by having such a high profile and the Netflix show.He also said that without that the team may have just tried to replace the cheerleaders because there are many people who would take jobs in the entertainment industry at low pay“So you see a lot of that inequality of compensation in any sort of artistic or entertainment field where you have lots of people clamoring to get into it and maybe being unpaid or very poorly paid to do so,” Chen said.The second season of Netflix’s America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, which aired in 2025, brought fresh attention to the squad’s pay negotiations.During the series, a cheerleader said members had received a 400% pay increase. The raise followed negotiations over compensation and represented another major jump after the 2019 settlement.Reports surrounding the 2025 increase highlighted how sharply cheerleader pay had changed over several years. Still, the raise and the newly recognized union represent two separate developments. The earlier increase improved compensation, while union recognition creates a formal structure for future negotiations.The Cowboys are one of the most valuable franchises in professional sports, according to Forbes. Their cheerleaders also enjoy international recognition, strengthened by decades of performances and the Netflix series.Yet the squad’s popularity has not removed questions about compensation and working conditions.The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are not the first NFL cheerleading squad to pursue union representation. The Buffalo Jills, who cheered for the Buffalo Bills, won the right to unionize in 1995. The squad later disbanded after a 2014 lawsuit raised allegations involving unpaid work and sexual harassment.After years of pay disputes and a major increase in 2025, the cheerleaders now have a formal route to negotiate their employment terms. What comes out of those talks will determine how much the union changes their working lives.
Article Summary: Dallas Cowboys recognize cheerleaders’ union after years of pay concerns. Move comes after Netflix series America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders brought their working lives and financial struggles to a wider audience. In 2018, former Cowboys cheerleader Erica Wilkins filed a lawsuit over her pay.

Article Title: Mohsin Naqvi-led PCB plans new Hong Kong Sixes-style tournament to expand cricket's reach
Article Text:
Mohsin Naqvi (PTI Photo)

PSL Sixes could reach smaller cities

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), led by Mohsin Naqvi, is exploring plans to launch a new six-a-side cricket tournament called PSL Sixes. The idea is to make cricket more entertaining for fans while expanding the reach of the Pakistan Super League (PSL).The proposal comes after Pakistan withdrew from the World Championship of Legends (WCL) 2026 amid tensions with India.Speaking on a PSL podcast, league chief executive Salman Naseer confirmed that the tournament is still being discussed and no final decision has been made."Nothing is finalised, but there are some exciting plans, and one of them is a sixes tournament, called the PSL Sixes, which will be in the off-season. We will look into the prospect of launching this tournament, and it will be very exciting, entertaining and engaging for the fans when it becomes a recurring feature," he said.The PCB is also considering taking the competition to smaller stadiums and cities where regular PSL matches have not been held. This could help more fans watch live cricket and give the tournament a wider audience."Maybe even going to the smaller stadiums and smaller cities, where we have not been able to take the PSL, and we know the fans are eager to watch cricket.So, a smaller event might be doable, which is what we are exploring," he added.Unlike the Hong Kong Sixes, which features teams representing different countries, the proposed PSL Sixes is expected to follow a franchise-based format, with teams representing cities and regions in Pakistan.Pakistan have been highly successful in the Hong Kong Sixes, winning the tournament six times since it began in 1992. They are also the defending champions, with the next edition scheduled for October 31 and November 1.Meanwhile, the PCB has reportedly refused permission for Pakistan's over-50s team to travel to India for the International Masters Cricket World Cup in January next year. The team had won the previous edition in Sri Lanka, but the board informed the Pakistan Veterans Cricket Association that it could not travel to India for the upcoming tournament.

Article Title: 18-year-old Anahat Singh's historic run at Silicon Valley Open comes to an end
Article Text:
Anahat Singh

Sivasangari praises Anahat’s talent

Anahat creates history despite exit

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s young squash star Anahat Singh saw her run at the Silicon Valley Open come to an end after losing 3-1 to Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam on Friday (local time) in Redwood City.The 18-year-old started strongly, winning the opening game 11-5. However, Sivasangari bounced back to take the next three games 11-6, 11-4 and 11-7, securing a 3-1 victory and a place in the final.The Malaysian had also beaten Anahat in the women’s singles final at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, denying the Indian a gold medal.After the match, Sivasangari praised Anahat’s skills and said the young Indian was already among the leading players despite her age. She explained that finding her accuracy helped her recover after a slow start and take control of the contest.“Anahat is very talented and so dangerous. She’s definitely amongst the top girls now, and she’s still so young. Coming into today’s match, I started a bit slow but got myself back into it, and I’m glad with the way I finished it. Obviously it’s easy to fall into her game; it wasn’t really a ‘who’s playing the best shot’ kind of game, but I needed ot find my accuracy and once I found that, the game changed.I could have done a few things a bit better, but overall I’m happy with the performance,” she said, as quoted by the PSA website.Although her campaign ended in the semifinals, Anahat had an impressive tournament. Earlier, she defeated eight-time world champion Nour ElSherbini in Round 2.She beat world No. 14 Salma Hany 3-2 in a 42-minute quarterfinal, winning 4-11, 11-8, 4-11, 11-2 and 11-5.That victory made her the first Indian woman squash player since 2019 to reach the semifinals of a PSA Tour Gold-level event.It was also her first semifinal appearance at this level, marking an important milestone in her young career.Despite the defeat, Anahat’s performance highlighted her growing presence in international squash, while Sivasangari once again proved a tough opponent for the Indian teenager.
Article Summary: Anahat Singh loses 3-1 to Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam at Silicon Valley Open. The 18-year-old was the first Indian woman squash player to reach the semifinals of a PSA Tour Gold-level event. It was her first semifinal appearance at this level.

Article Title: CJP activists’ detention puts spotlight on how SEMs play a crucial role
Article Text:
Recent observations by the Delhi HC have scrutinized the actions of these magistrates concerning the detainment of CJP activists

Who are SEMs?

How are they different from judicial magistrates?

When can an SEM ask someone to furnish a peace bond ?

Procedure: Under Section 130, the magistrate must issue a written order explaining the basis for the proceedings, the proposed bond amount, its duration and the number of sureties required.

Duration: A peace bond can be required for up to one year, and the amount must not be excessive.

Can it be challenged? The person must be given an opportunity to explain why they should not be required to furnish the bond. The magistrate then conducts an inquiry under Section 135.

When can an SEM order detention?

During inquiry: Under Section 135(3), an SEM may require immediate security if necessary to prevent a breach of peace or danger to public safety. If the person fails to furnish it, they may be detained until the inquiry concludes.

After inquiry: Under Section 136, the magistrate can order security if the inquiry establishes it is necessary. Under Section 137, the person must be discharged if the need for security isn’t established.

Failure to furnish security: Section 141 provides for imprisonment in specified circumstances, including failure to furnish security after a final order or breach of a qualifying bond.

Who can stand as a surety?

“Photograph mismatch”: The first surety’s photograph on the bond allegedly didn’t match his Aadhaar

“Insufficient identity proof”: He reportedly failed to produce another valid ID and gave unsatisfactory answers during questioning

“Lack of basic details”: The second surety couldn’t provide basic information, including the parentage and address of Saurav Das, for whom she stood as surety

“Insufficient control”: The SEM concluded the sureties didn’t have sufficient control over the activists to ensure their presence when required





NEW DELHI: Though a common feature in cases involving summary or preventive detention by police, the powers of special executive magistrates (SEMs) have come into focus due to their prominent role in deciding if those involved in recent protests rocking Delhi are released or remain behind bars.A person not familiar with the rare, overlapping functions and powers of the executive and judiciary may conclude SEMs are a rung of the judiciary where a person picked up by police is produced within 24 hours.However, the reality is more complex, since the law empowers govt officials, mostly police officers, to exercise magisterial powers in cases of detention, where they can even remand a detainee to judicial custody, as happened in the case of CJP’s Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.Wednesday was the first time decisions taken by SEMs came under judicial scrutiny of any kind, when Delhi HC heard the CJP members’ plea. The court, however, refused to go into merits.Under Section 15 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), state govts can appoint executive magistrates or police officers of at least superintendent of police rank as SEMs for specific areas, periods or duties.Depending on state-specific notifications, these officers can also be deputy collectors or tehsildars or senior police officers of ACP rank.Their primary role is to take preventive measures to maintain public order and stop anticipated breaches of peace.Under BNSS Section 9, the state govt establishes courts of judicial magistrates in consultation with HC, which appoints their presiding officers. Judicial magistrates deal with criminal cases and trials while SEMs exercise executive powers, including initiating preventive proceedings.SEMs cannot conduct criminal trials or convict people through these proceedings, but are authorised to release or grant police or judicial remand. Under the earlier Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), the corresponding provision for SEMs was Section 21.Under Section 126, an SEM can initiate proceedings if there is sufficient ground to believe a person is likely to breach the peace or disturb public tranquillity.Separately, Section 163 allows an executive magistrate to issue urgent orders to prevent specified dangers or disturbances, including restricting public gatherings when legal conditions are met.Detention is not automatic once proceedings begin.A surety undertakes responsibility under a bond to help ensure the person concerned meets its conditions. Under Section 140, an SEM can reject a surety found unfit, but must conduct an inquiry, give the parties a reasonable opportunity to be heard and record reasons in writing.In Das and Ranka’s case, the SEM rejected fresh sureties over reported “discrepancies” in identification documents and missing details.
Article Summary: The powers of special executive magistrates (SEMs) have come into focus due to their prominent role in deciding if those involved in recent protests are released or remain behind bars. Wednesday was the first time decisions taken by SEMs came under judicial scrutiny of any kind, when Delhi HC heard the CJP members’ plea.

Article Title: 'I clean, they dirty faster': MP's Bittu Tabahi may quit cleaning river forever
Article Text:
Photo: @bittu_tabahi/ Instagram

Bittu cleaned river stretch alone, larger civic failure is now making him fight losing battle





BHOPAL: Madhya Pradesh's 20-year-old college student Surendra Singh Choudhary-better known to the country as "Bittu Tabahi"-is a dejected man. Bittu, who hogged international limelight for single-handedly cleaning up a stretch of Ajnar river in Rajgarh's Biaora, says every time he cleans up the river, people dump garbage back into it-sometimes almost immediately. The situation worsened after Dussehra, when fresh waste accumulated along the banks he had worked so hard to restore."I have been working to clean this river for the past year. Every time I have cleaned it, people have dirtied it again," he said, his voice heavy with disappointment. "I am starting to lose heart.""I think I should focus on my studies," Bittu said.I don't believe I will be able to continue cleaning the Ajnar river any longer."The statement marks a troubling turn for a campaign that became a symbol of individual environmental action. Bittu's central argument remains simple: removing garbage is only temporary if people continue to throw waste into the river. Lasting change, he believes, requires citizens to stop littering in the first place.Ajnar, which flows through Biaora in Rajgarh district, had long been treated as an open dumping ground.Passers-by reportedly covered their mouths with cloth to escape its stench. Bittu began cleaning a stretch of the river on Jan 26, initially with a few friends, but soon found himself working alone, armed with little more than basic tools and determination.There was no govt order, no funding and no formal campaign behind his effort. He used his own money for supplies, entered foul water despite not knowing how to swim, and removed waste bag by bag. For a while, the results were visible. The stretch Bittu cleaned became noticeably clearer, and his videos earned praise from across India and abroad.But that recognition has not stopped the river from being littered again. His frustration deepened after he installed two dustbins along the riverbank, hoping residents and visitors would dispose of waste responsibly. One of the bins later went missing. Bittu clarified that the dustbins were meant for public use, not personal convenience.During another clean-up, conducted with the local Nagar Palika team, Bittu found an Indian national flag among the waste. He used the moment to ask a question that has become central to his campaign: "When will we understand our responsibility?"Those who have followed Bittu's work describe a young volunteer whose energy was once extraordinary. He cleaned without machinery, faced health risks and snake encounters, and continued even after criticism. But repeated relapse of pollution has begun to test that resolve. Bittu's exhaustion highlights a larger civic failure. A single student can clean a river, but he cannot police a town's habits, provide permanent waste infra, or sustain a clean-up alone.
Article Summary: Surendra Singh Choudhary, known as "Bittu Tabahi," is a 20-year-old college student from Madhya Pradesh. Bittu hogged international limelight for single- handedly cleaning up a stretch of Ajnar river in Rajgarh's Biaora. He says every time he cleans up the river, people dump garbage back into it.

Article Title: Cheered in Chhota Udepur, but Vadodara shuts stage to Muslim who played Lakshmana for 14 years
Article Text:
Abid Sheikh, an actor in Vadodara, was excluded from performing in Ram Leela due to his religion.





VADODARA: On Dussehra , Abid Sheikh drew applause in tribal Chhota Udepur for bringing the characters of Kevat and Meghnad alive on stage in a Ram Leela.In Vadodara, however, the city he calls home, the 39-year-old was unable to perform in the Ram Leela he had been associated with for nearly 14 years, after objections to his participation over his religion by right-wing groups.The contrast has left Sheikh, a science graduate who grew up fascinated by the Ramayana, grappling with an unexpected rejection from a tradition that had become an integral part of his life.For years, Sheikh played Laxman and Bharat in the Ram Leela organised by the North India Cultural Association (NICA) at Polo Ground during Dussehra. He learnt his dialogues, rehearsed for weeks and earned appreciation from audiences. His family, too, shared his commitment, giving up non-vegetarian food during the rehearsal period until the festival concluded.But the welcome he had long received on stage in Vadodara changed last year when some right-wing activists turned up during rehearsals and objected to his casting because he was a Muslim.“I played different roles in Ram Leela for around 14 years and was showered with love and appreciation by the audience.Last year, some activists suddenly turned up during rehearsals and objected to my casting because of my religion. I was shocked, as I never expected this,” Sheikh told TOI.He said the activists pressured the organisers to drop him. This year, he was not invited to perform in the Vadodara production.“Ram Leela had become a part of my life, but they did not want me anywhere near the stage,” he said.The rejection was particularly painful because his association with the epic began in childhood. After watching a cartoon based on the Ramayana, Sheikh developed a fascination for Laxman. An opportunity to perform in a school Ram Leela gave him his first taste of acting, and he continued playing characters from the epic for years.Shashikant Das, director, NICA, told TOI: “Sheikh is such a good actor and he is an ardent fan of Ramayan. He chants Hanuman Chalisa. But Bajrang Dal activists came last year and protested against his role. I argued and fought in Sheikh’s defence.”“But the management came under pressure. So, this time he wasn’t invited for the Ram Leela. It’s sad that we lost a good actor like him,” Das said and pointed out that those preparing the giant effigies of Ravana, Meghnad and Kumbhakarna at Polo Ground are also Muslim artists from Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Abid Sheikh, an actor in Vadodara, was excluded from performing in Ram Leela due to his religion. Right-wing activists turned up during rehearsals and objected to his casting because he was a Muslim. He said the activists pressured the organisers to drop him.

Article Title: ‘You did nothing wrong’: Faf du Plessis reveals message to Steve Smith during Sandpapergate
Article Text:
File Pic: Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft

‘We're behind you’: Faf's message to Smith

Smith had stood by Faf during ‘ Mintgate ’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has recalled reaching out to Steve Smith during the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering controversy, questioning why the Australian had taken responsibility for the incident while expressing solidarity with a rival who had previously stood by him during his own ball-tampering scandal.Speaking on Cricinfo’s Cricketers on Cricketers, du Plessis said Smith’s response to the controversy had reminded him of the media storm he faced in 2016, when he was accused of using residue from a sweet to alter the condition of the ball during a Test against Australia in Hobart.Smith, Australia's captain at the time, was at the centre of a major controversy during the 2018 tour of South Africa after Cameron Bancroft was caught attempting to alter the ball's condition with sandpaper in the Cape Town Test. Smith and vice-captain David Warner were also found guilty of their roles in the incident."Steve came out at the end of the day [in Cape Town in 2018] saying: 'I take responsibility.' And we were like: 'Why are you taking responsibility? You did nothing wrong,'" du Plessis said.Du Plessis said he immediately empathised with Smith as the controversy escalated and the Australian faced intense media scrutiny. Drawing parallels with his own experience, the former South African skipper sent Smith a message of support, assuring him that he understood the pressure he was going through."And then everything just exploded in terms of the media and how he was being put under pressure. Straight away, I was like: this is not his doing. This is the same thing [as my ball-tampering charge]. I remember sending a message and saying: 'Listen, I'm so sorry you are going through this. Just be strong. It's going to be a hell for a week or so and then it will probably blow over.' Never knowing that it was going to be a year for him to go through. But just saying… we're behind you. We understand you did nothing wrong. So if you need anything from us, we're here," he told Cricinfo.The former South Africa captain admitted he had not anticipated the severity of the punishment that would follow, with Cricket Australia eventually imposing one-year suspensions on Smith and Warner and removing Smith from the captaincy. Bancroft received a nine-month ban, while the International Cricket Council handed Smith a one-Test suspension.Du Plessis also recalled how Smith had defended him during the 2016 Hobart controversy, when accusations of cheating began to spread internationally. The South African said the situation had initially appeared relatively minor to his dressing room, before the growing media attention turned it into a major issue."At the time, in our dressing room, honestly, we thought nothing had happened badly. But cameras [were] everywhere. And it just got built up into this thing now. All of a sudden, I was in real trouble. It was going around the world, people saying, 'Cheating.' That weighs heavy on you,” he said.According to du Plessis, Smith was asked about the allegations against the South African and chose to defend him, despite the pressure surrounding the issue.“He was asked: What are your thoughts on Faf du Plessis and Mintgate, and it's terrible, he's cheating. And he's like, no, he's not. He's just shining the ball. I've been on many teams where we shine the ball, we use different sweets. We were listening to it on the TV and literally everyone in our group was like, 'Wow, he doesn't have to do that.' That was a choice where he went: I'm going to choose probably the human, the right thing, versus the pressure thing. That was amazing for me to see. I remember just saying that that meant a lot to the South African team and the respect that we got for Steve Smith that day," he added.Du Plessis said Smith's willingness to speak up when he could have simply criticised his rival left a lasting impression on the South African camp.
Article Summary: Faf du Plessis has recalled reaching out to Steve Smith during the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering controversy. The former South African skipper said he empathised with Smith as the controversy escalated and the Australian faced intense media scrutiny. Smith had stood by Faf during'Mintgate' in 2016.

Article Title: As foam builds up in Yamuna, questions raised over how work was allotted
Article Text:
A defoaming operation is set to begin in Yamuna near Kalindi Kunj, with equipment already in place.





NEW DELHI: A tanker, machinery, safety jackets and other equipment for the anti-foam operation for Yamuna near Kalindi Kunj is all set to go. A colourful tent is also in place. A few metres away, white foam, which indicates high concentration of pollutants, is building up in the river channel, waiting for a defoaming solution that can cut through it.The only glitch is the questions raised by the timeline of work allocation.Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has alleged that even before the tender bids for the work were opened. In a news conference Thursday, the party alleged that the process was structured to favour a "pre-determined contractor". It also alleged that three days before the tender bids were opened, the contractor had already started to set up equipment at the site.As per documents, four tenders were floated for the defoaming exercise. These were supposed to be opened on Oct 21 and 22 (Wednesday and Thursday).During a visit, TOI found tents set up and divided into three sections. Equipment and machinery, along with a tanker of the Delhi Jal Board were present on site. The defoaming chemicals, those present on the site said, were yet to arrive. The contractor, ICON Instruments Company, refused to comment on the controversy and redirected qu-estions to Delhi Jal Board (DJB) officials, stating that the work was being handled by them.Workers on site confirmed that the camp was set up five days ago.Responding to the allegations, DJB assistant chemist Sandeep Verma said, "We have been carrying out the defoaming process since 2022. DJB conducts a defoaming campaign every year, and we successfully carried it out in 2023 as well. This ghat was not previously included in the list of designated ghats but a defoaming campaign was conducted here last year as well. All the infrastructure you currently see here belongs to DJB. The firm that carried out the work last year had this equipment available and it was in our stock. We have issued a tender worth Rs 80 lakh, plus applicable taxes, for this work."During the spot visit, TOI found foam visible on the water and plastic, polythene and other waste strewn across the riverbank. Discarded puja material, idols of deities, clothes and other garbage had accumulated along the banks.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has alleged that the process was structured to favour a "pre-determined contractor" The contractor, ICON Instruments Company, refused to comment on the controversy and redirected qu-estions to Delhi Jal Board (DJB) officials.

Article Title: FBI detains gangster Himanshu Bhau, India may get custody soon
Article Text:
Gangsters Himanshu Bhau and Neeraj Faridpuria in custody in US

Himanshu's major cirmes





NEW DELHI: Himanshu Bhau, one of north India's most wanted gangsters, is learnt to have been detained in the US, after a four-year-long manhunt. Subject of a red notice from the Interpol, Bhau, a rival of Lawrence Bishnoi group, is wanted for multiple cases off shootings, killings and multi-crore extortions in Delhi and Haryana.Bhau, sources said, was apprehended by FBI in Las Vegas/Nevada region following inputs from Indian agencies. He is likely to be handed over to Indian law enforcement agencies, who have been chasing him since 2022, in the coming days, sources said.In his early twenties, Bhau is one of north India's most notorious young fugitives, heading an organised crime syndicate. He has been a headache for cops in Delhi, Haryana and Rajasthan with back-to-back killings, including three sensational murders in Delhi, this year."He belongs to Ritoli in the Rohtak district of Haryana and had got involved in crimes while still in school. He first entered police records in 2020 following a botched killing attempt involving a localized dispute in his native village," an investigator recalled.Since he was a minor at the time of apprehension, cops detained him and sent him to a juvenile observation home in Hisar. However, his stay there was brief; he engineered an audacious escape from the facility, casting aside any prospect of rehabilitation and plunging headfirst into a career of violent crime that soon expanded far beyond rural Haryana.Operating in close coordination with seasoned syndicates, including the Neeraj Bawana and Naveen Bali gangs, Bhau rapidly built a formidable network spanning Rohtak, Jhunjhunu, Sonipat, and the National Capital Region of Delhi.As law enforcement agencies closed in on his local footprints, including a series of high-profile murders in his home district in March 2022, he managed to orchestrate an escape from the country."In 2022, he executed three killings in a span of 24 days in March. The same year, using a passport obtained through fraudulent documents, Bhau slipped across international borders, initially fleeing to Dubai before moving on to European safe havens like Portugal, from where he continued to remotely direct his syndicate," said an investigator.Despite being a fugitive with Red Corner Notices and heavy cash rewards issued by multiple police jurisdictions and the National Investigation Agency, he leveraged encrypted messaging applications to command local shooters.He is suspected to have reached US through the "Dunkey Route" in late 2024-early 2025.His syndicate has claimed responsibility for a string of high-profile shootings, extortions, and contract killings that terrorised businessmen and shook law enforcement.Among his syndicate's most brazen operations was the daring killing of a rival at a prominent fast-food chain outlet in West Delhi's Rajouri Garden.His network has also targeted commercial establishments, unleashing dozens of rounds of gunfire at car showrooms in Naraina and Tilak Nagar alongside multi-million rupee extortion demands directed at builders, real estate developers, and local traders across Delhi-NCR.
Article Summary: Himanshu Bhau, one of north India's most wanted gangsters, is learnt to have been detained in the US. Subject of a red notice from the Interpol, Bhau is wanted for multiple cases off shootings, killings and multi-crore extortions. He is likely to be handed over to Indian law enforcement agencies, who have been chasing him since 2022, in the coming days.
