Article Title: Minor’s parent fined Rs 15,000 over fake AI leopard photo
Article Text:
The department warned that using technology to spread false information about wildlife could invite legal action

Kolhapur

:





The forest department has fined the parent of a minor Rs 15,000 for circulating an AI-generated fake image of a leopard sighting in the Kalamba-Pachgaon area adjoining Kolhapur city, triggering panic among residents.On Friday, Oct 16, Sagar Dalvi, a Pachgaon gram panchayat member, alerted the forest department about a leopard allegedly spotted at Aptemala in Pachgaon. He also forwarded a photo he had received on his mobile phone. Forest officials and the wildlife rapid rescue team rushed to the spot but found no evidence of a leopard.Range Forest Officer Nandkumar Nalawade said an investigation revealed that a minor boy from Pachgaon had created the image using an AI app as a prank on his friends and circulated it on social media.“During investigation, it was revealed that a minor boy from the Pachgaon village had circulated the photo on social media. When our team questioned the boy, he lied about seeing a leopard out of fear. However, upon further questioning, he confessed that he had created a fake photo of the leopard with the help of an AI app to prank his friends and had made it viral. Later, the boy’s parents also admitted that this incident had happened unknowingly.A nuisance fine of Rs 15,000 was collected from the parent so that such thing won’t be repeated in future,” Nalawade said.The department warned that using technology to spread false information about wildlife could invite legal action.“Misusing technology to spread false news about wildlife behaviour in this way can lead to legal action. Citizens are appealed not to believe such rumours and not to forward any photos or messages without verifying them,” Nalawade added.The action was taken under the guidance of Deputy Conservator of Forests Dhairyasheel Patil and Assistant Conservator of Forests Priyanka Dalvi.
Article Summary: The forest department has fined the parent of a minor Rs 15,000 for circulating an AI-generated fake image of a leopard sighting. The image triggered panic among residents in the Kalamba-Pachgaon area adjoining Kolhapur city. The department warned that using technology to spread false information about wildlife could invite legal action.

Article Title: Poland PM wishes to visit refugee museum at Valivade, says ex-Rajya Sabha member Sambhajiraje
Article Text:
Silver photo frame of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj gifted to Prime Minister Tusk by Sambhajiraje Chhatrapati

Kolhapur

:





“Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk has expressed a wish to visit Valivade’s Museum For Humanity and Peace, being developed to preserve the memories of World War II refugees,” said ex-Rajya Sabha MP Sambhajiraje Chhatrapati after meeting Tusk in Bengaluru on Friday morning.Polish PM was on a three-day visit to India and Bengaluru was his last stop. Sambhajiraje, who is leading Maharashtra’s team to develop the museum with contributions from Poles, was invited to interact with Tusk and provide details of the project. At Valivade near Kolhapur city, thousands of Polish refugees, who left their country after the German and then Russian invasions, were sheltered by Sambhajiraje’s grandfather for four years till 1948.“Poland’s PM wishes to visit Valivade in early 2027. We are planning a grand opening for the museum and he expressed interest in the opening event. We spoke on various issues and I projected Kolhapur’s potential as an investment hub. Beyond historic ties we have with Poland, we also agreed to explore trade, business, education, culture, tourism and other avenues,” said the ex-Rajya Sabha MP.In Aug, Polish MP Kinga Gajewska led a delegation to Kolhapur to hand over memories collected from the families of refugees.These memories and the artefacts gifted by Poland govt will be displayed in the museum, which is being developed in the same barracks where refugees used to live.Polish PM told Sambhajiraje that the museum will be a symbol of peace and humanity and will serve as an inspiration for future generations to strive for human values. Indian and Polish ambassadors of both countries were present for the meeting.
Article Summary: Polish PM was on a three-day visit to India and Bengaluru was his last stop. Thousands of Polish refugees, who left their country after the German and then Russian invasions, were sheltered by Sambhajiraje’s grandfather for four years till 1948.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Bengaluru artistes bring ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ to life at Dombivli Navratri festival
Article Text:
Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.





DOMBIVLI: A theatrical portrayal of Goddess Durga’s battle against demon Mahishasura offered Dombivli residents a glimpse into India’s traditional performing arts during the Sharadiya Navratri festival.Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale of the goddess’s victory to life.The programme was organised as part of the Navratri celebrations hosted by the Dr Shrikant Shinde Foundation and Shri Navdurga Yuva Mandal at the DNC school grounds in Dombivli East.Kalyan MP Dr Shrikant Shinde, who attended the event, stressed the importance of preserving and promoting traditional art forms that reflect India's cultural heritage.“Artistic performances that preserve our culture and traditions are important. They need encouragement and support so that this rich heritage can be passed on to future generations,” Shinde said.The presentation centred on the story of Mahishasura, whose tyranny threatened the world until Goddess Durga took the form of Mahishasuramardini to defeat him.Through a combination of theatrical expression, dance and devotional elements, the Bengaluru artistes depicted the goddess’s strength and the victory of righteousness over evil.Organisers said the festival seeks to go beyond religious rituals by providing a platform for India's diverse cultural and spiritual traditions. Alongside devotional activities, the programme features performances showcasing different forms of traditional art.At a time when modern entertainment platforms are increasingly popular, such performances offer an opportunity to introduce younger audiences to India's mythological stories and traditional artistic expressions.They also help preserve cultural practices that have been passed down through generations.The Navratri festival has included a range of religious and cultural programmes, including the Navkundatmak Sahasrachandi Mahayag, Haripath, bhajan sessions and devotional music.The organisers have sought to combine religious observances with cultural activities to give visitors a wider experience of the festival.The ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ presentation added a distinctive dimension to this year's celebrations, highlighting the role of traditional theatre in keeping India's mythological narratives and performing arts alive.
Article Summary: Bengaluru artistes presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil. The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale to life.

Article Title: Rush hour traffic snarls on Sinhagad Road lead to delays; commuters irked; demand grows to start Sun City-Karvenagar bridge
Article Text:
Representative photo

Pune:





A 6-km-long stretch of Sinhagad Road witnessed a massive traffic jam during rush hours on Friday morning, leading to delays with many office-goers saying vehicles moved at a snail’s pace on the section between Panmala chowk and Dhayari flyover.Work on a power supply line near the Ganeshmala area led to such an unprecedented traffic jam, said police, adding that the snarl created huge chaos at the Rajaram bridge junction. The entire flyover and also a stretch of the road under the flyover witnessed slow-moving traffic.Traffic police personnel deployed additional manpower at the Rajaram bridge chowk to clear the chaos. Officials said a team of 12 personnel was deployed at various locations between Ganeshmala chowk and Dhayri main chowk to manage the traffic.Regular commuters in the Sinhagad Road area have claimed that the road has been witnessing repeated traffic snarls. A similar problem was faced on Thursday evening too. Traffic problems in the area have not been resolved despite visits by officials of Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) and mayor Manjusha Nagpure.Mahesh Pokale, a local activist, said PMC has constructed two flyovers on Sinhagad Road but the traffic problems still persist.“It is the responsibility of the civic administration to find solutions to the traffic jams and clearing bottlenecks. Regular commuters are facing a lot of hardships owing to overall mismanagement,” he said.Local activist Vinit Dhayarkar said the civic administration should give a detailed explanation of the steps taken so far to manage increasing traffic on Sinhagad Road. He said, “We have five main demands. The administration should not take up any road digging work without intimation and alternate traffic plans. The mayor had asked for a detailed traffic survey. The administration should declare findings of the survey and action taken on suggestions. They should also clear all encroachments obstructing smooth vehicular flow. Prepare a plan to clear the bottleneck at Dhayari phata and Dhayari gaon.”The residents have also demanded that the administration open the Sun City to Karvenagar bridge and widen the Rajaram bridge to decentralise the traffic flow and reduce dependency on the existing Rajaram bridge. The work on Sun City to Karvenagar bridge is in the last stages, as the approach roads to the bridge are yet to be developed to full capacity, said a PMC official.
Article Summary: A 6-km-long stretch of Sinhagad Road witnessed a massive traffic jam during rush hours on Friday morning. Many office-goers said vehicles moved at a snail's pace on the section between Panmala chowk and Dhayari flyover. A similar problem was faced on Thursday evening too.

Article Title: 3 premature babies beat odds at AIIMS-Nagpur, 1 weighed just 480g
Article Text:
AIIMS

Nagpur:





Three extremely premature babies, including one who weighed less than half a kilogram at birth, have beaten the odds to survive and return home, bringing immense joy to their families.Born months before the standard 40-week pregnancy term, the fragile infants needed intensive care to overcome life-threatening complications associated with extreme prematurity.Two were born at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Nagpur and admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) immediately after birth, while the third was brought to the hospital in critical condition on the fourth day of life. All three were discharged after nearly three months of intensive care.“These babies were born at the very edge of survival, and every day of their journey was a triumph of teamwork,” said Dr Prashant Joshi, executive director of AIIMS Nagpur.According to hospital adminsitration, one infant, born at just 24 weeks of gestation and weighing 600 grams, is the youngest survivor by gestational age ever cared for at the hospital’s NICU.Another, weighing a mere 480 grams at birth, is the smallest survivor by birth weight treated at the facility.The babies required prolonged breathing support and round-the-clock care as they battled severe complications, including patent ductus arteriosus (a heart vessel that fails to close after birth), retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), an eye disorder, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia, a chronic lung disease. A multidisciplinary team managed these complications through vigilant monitoring and timely intervention, helping the infants gradually gain strength.The third baby, born at 26 weeks and weighing just 630 grams, was brought to AIIMS Nagpur in critical condition. The infant’s survival holds special significance for the family: the mother’s eighth pregnancy followed the devastating loss of seven previous pregnancies. Desperate to save her baby, she travelled from outside Maharashtra to seek specialised care at the institute. After weeks of treatment and close monitoring, the baby recovered and was discharged in good health, doctors said.Faculty members from the department of neonatology — Dr Nishant Banait, Dr Sanjana Somanath, Dr Amit Kumar and Dr Arun Edwin — worked alongside resident doctors, nursing officers and support staff throughout the infants’ treatment.“For infants this small, every gram and every hour matters. Their recovery was possible because doctors, nurses, and support staff worked as one team, and because the parents trusted us and stayed with their babies through the long weeks of care,” said Dr Banait.Congratulating the neonatology team, Joshi said the institute remained committed to ensuring that the smallest and most vulnerable newborns received world-class care, regardless of where they came from.
Article Summary: Three extremely premature babies, including one who weighed less than half a kilogram at birth, have beaten the odds to survive and return home. Born months before the standard 40-week pregnancy term, the fragile infants needed intensive care to overcome life-threatening complications associated with extreme prematurity. All three were discharged after nearly three months of intensive care.

Article Title: Preparations at Ramkund in full swing for Oct 31 Dhwajarohan
Article Text:
Preparations are under way at Ramkund as the stage is set for the Simhastha Kumbh Mela flag-hoisting ceremony on Oct 31

Nashik

:





Preparations for the Dhwajarohan ceremony on Oct 31 are in the final stretch, with Nashik Municipal Corporation (NMC) making extensive arrangements at Ramkund and the adjoining Godaghat to manage the expected influx of sadhus, pilgrims and devotees.President Droupadi Murmu is expected to attend the flag-hoisting ceremony and the Goda aarti on the right bank of Godavari near Ramkund. “A dedicated stage is being readied for the event, while most infrastructure works at the venue have already been completed,” an official said.According to civic officials, the remaining works are likely to be wrapped up by Saturday. NMC has also sought approval from Kumbh Mela Authority for facilities proposed for sadhus and pilgrims attending the ceremony.NMC will deploy doctors and health personnel at the venue, backed by six ambulances for immediate medical response, to strengthen emergency preparedness. “Nearby civic-run Indira Gandhi Hospital and Zakir Hussain Hospital will remain on alert, while beds are also being reserved at two leading private hospitals as a precautionary measure,” the official said.Special city bus services will operate from various parts of Nashik to Ramkund on Oct 31 to ease the movement of devotees attending the Dhwajarohan and evening aarti.“We have reviewed arrangements at the ghats and inspected the two flagpoles installed for the ceremony. A 51-foot dhwajstambh has been installed for the Kumbh Mela flag, while a 31-foot dhwajstambh will carry the Dharma Dhwaj of the Nashik Purohit Sangh,” another NMC official said.In the lead-up to the event, the banks of Godavari will host a mass Shankhanaad programme on Sunday, where more than 500 participants are expected to simultaneously blow conch shells in an attempt to set a world record. The spectacle is also planned as a key attraction during the Oct 31 celebrations.
Article Summary: President Droupadi Murmu is expected to attend the flag-hoisting ceremony and the Goda aarti on the right bank of Godavari near Ramkund. A dedicated stage is being readied for the event, while most infrastructure works at the venue have already been completed.
